    • consentPage

      @RequestMapping(method=GET, value="/oauth2/consent", produces="text/html") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<String> consentPage(@NotNull @Size(min=1) @Valid @RequestParam(value="client_id",required=true) @NotNull @Size(min=1) @Valid String clientId, @NotNull @Valid @RequestParam(value="scope",required=true) @NotNull @Valid String scope, @NotNull @Size(min=1) @Valid @RequestParam(value="state",required=true) @NotNull @Size(min=1) @Valid String state, @Size(max=32) @Valid @RequestParam(value="user_code",required=false) @Nullable @Size(max=32) @Valid String userCode)
      GET /oauth2/consent : Renders the consent page Renders the page the authorization endpoint redirects to when a client needs the user's approval: the client, the requested scopes (as checkboxes, checked by default) and the scopes granted earlier. The decision is posted to the authorization endpoint (POST /oauth2/authorize), or to the device verification endpoint for a device, never to this operation.
      Parameters:
      clientId - Identifier of the registered client that asks for access. (required)
      scope - Requested scopes, space delimited as in the authorization request. (required)
      state - State the authorization endpoint generated for the consent step, posted back with the decision. (required)
      userCode - Present when the consent is asked for a device (OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant): the user code of the request. The decision is then posted to the device verification endpoint (POST /oauth2/device_verification) instead, with this code. (optional)
      Returns:
      The consent page. (status code 200) or The client is unknown or a parameter is missing; the error page is rendered, without any detail of the failure. (status code 400)
